added_claims.quote: achieved at least 150 tokens per second with p90 TTFT at most two seconds
added_claims.statement: A second serving-cost comparison uses only configurations tested at >=150 tokens/sec with p90 time-to-first-token of at most two seconds.

added_claims.quote: KV compression reduces the cached state stored per token, and sparse attention reduces how much of that state each attention operation reads
added_claims.statement: GLM 5.2/5.3 reduces the cost of retaining conversation history in two ways: KV compression (less cached state per token) and sparse attention (less of that state read per attention operation).

added_claims.quote: For every token, it has 1 shared expert and is routed through 8 out of 256 experts, which is sparsity 32.
added_claims.statement: GLM-5 routes each token through 1 shared expert plus 8 of 256 experts, giving sparsity of 32.

added_claims.quote: configures MHA mode for sequence length 2K to about 5K for data parallel, and 2K to about 77K for tensor parallel
added_claims.statement: vLLM configures MHA mode for sequence lengths 2K to ~5K under data parallel and 2K to ~77K under tensor parallel.

added_claims.quote: the DeepSeek V3.2 configuration d = 512, r = 64, b = 2
added_claims.statement: DeepSeek V3.2 MLA configuration uses head dimension d=512, RoPE dimension r=64, and 2 bytes per parameter.

added_claims.quote: H800’s practical arithmetic intensity is 258.2 FLOP/B (Practical peak 865 TFLOP/s, 3.35 TB/s bandwidth, according to DeepSeek ), and plugging in the formula gives us H ~= 128.
added_claims.statement: H800's practical arithmetic intensity is 258.2 FLOP/B (865 TFLOP/s practical peak, 3.35 TB/s bandwidth per DeepSeek), implying the MLA head count ridge point is H~=128.

added_claims.quote: If we plug in GLM-5’s configuration (d = 512, r = 64, b = 2, H = 64), we get an arithmetic intensity of 120.8 FLOP/B.
added_claims.statement: GLM-5's MLA configuration (d=512, r=64, b=2, H=64) yields an arithmetic intensity of 120.8 FLOP/B.

added_claims.quote: GLM-5 increases the QK NoPE dimension from 128 to 192, as ablations show the configuration is superior under iso-FLOP and iso-parameter constraints
added_claims.statement: GLM-5 increases the QK NoPE dimension from 128 to 192, with ablations showing superiority under iso-FLOP and iso-parameter constraints.

added_claims.quote: This increases the SDPA head dimension from 192 to 256, which is still a 33% FLOP reduction after considering the head number reduction.
added_claims.statement: The change raises the SDPA head dimension from 192 to 256, still a 33% FLOP reduction after the head-count reduction.

added_claims.quote: Z.ai proposes IndexShare (aka IndexCache) in GLM-5.2, where every 4 DSA layers share one indexer
added_claims.statement: Z.ai's IndexShare (IndexCache), introduced in GLM-5.2, has every 4 DSA layers share one indexer to cut indexer latency cost.

added_claims.quote: For GLM5.3 on TileRT, AMD MI355X was supported first.
added_claims.statement: For GLM-5.3 on the TileRT low-latency inference engine, AMD's MI355X was the first supported hardware.
qualifiers: TileRT compiles decoding into a single persistent kernel

added_claims.quote: they merged more than ten expert models into a final model by training for about two days

added_claims.metric: training time to merge expert models

added_claims.quote: At the cost of computational overhead and doubling memory footprint, SAO replaces group-wise sampling with a value model
added_claims.statement: SAO's use of a separate value model doubles the memory footprint and adds computational overhead, trading these costs to mitigate GRPO latency issues

added_hypotheses.title: GLM-5 attention config suggests optimization for Chinese Moore Threads accelerators, not NVIDIA
added_hypotheses.premise_condition: If GLM-5's reduced query-head count (H=64, arithmetic intensity 120.8 FLOP/B) reflects design for domestic accelerators rather than H800

bottom_line_fact.text: GLM-5 uses H=64 query heads giving arithmetic intensity 120.8 FLOP/B, versus the H~=128 ridge point for H800 at 258.2 FLOP/B; SemiAnalysis suspects this targets Moore Threads MTT S4000 (~128 FLOP/B), corroborated by Moore Threads' GLM-5.3-Flash day-0 support.

bottom_line_inference.text: If leading Chinese open-weight models are being tuned to domestic silicon's roofline, it points to growing demand substitution away from NVIDIA/H800-class hardware toward Chinese accelerators, though the article offers only a circumstantial, inferential link.

source_implication.text: The article infers GLM-5 may be designed for different (likely Chinese) hardware than DeepSeek's H800-tuned configuration.

transmission_chain.text: Chinese model developers tune attention configurations to the arithmetic-intensity ridge point of specific accelerators.
If GLM-5 is optimized for Moore Threads MTT S4000, demand for that accelerator (and software support like day-0 GLM-5.3-Flash) could rise relative to NVIDIA parts.
Article does not quantify any earnings, revenue or share-shift effect for any named vendor.

near_term_view.text: No near-term catalyst stated; the inference rests on model architecture analysis and a collaboration (Moore Threads day-0 support).

structural_view.text: Model-hardware co-design tuned to domestic accelerator roofline could structurally support Chinese AI silicon demand over multi-year horizons.

opposing_explanations.text: The H=64 choice could reflect other design trade-offs (iso-FLOP/iso-parameter ablations favoring QK NoPE dimension) rather than hardware targeting, so the Moore Threads inference remains a suspicion.

unknowns: Whether GLM-5 is actually deployed on Moore Threads MTT S4000 in production volume
Whether any share shift away from NVIDIA/H800 materializes
Moore Threads is privately held / not clearly listed, so no direct listed-equity read; the hardware-targeting link is association, not demonstrated causation
disconfirming_observables: GLM-5.x models shown to run primarily on NVIDIA hardware at scale
No meaningful Moore Threads deployment or revenue tied to Z.ai
added_hypotheses.next_research_step: Verify whether Z.ai production serving of GLM-5.x runs on Moore Threads MTT S4000 and quantify any accelerator volume/share implications versus NVIDIA.
